summary.en-US: Send dollars to anyone by link. They tap, they get it, no app, no wallet, and they pay no gas.

description.en-US:
Send dollars to anyone with a link. Make it here, drop it into a chat or an email, and whoever opens it collects the money in their browser. The recipient needs no app, no wallet and no extension, and pays no gas: Lumenia's sponsor service covers the network fee.

Start in seconds: make a new account right in the extension with one password, and practice dollars are added for you. Or bring the Lumenia account you already have, with your email, a one-time code and your backup password. Back a new account up with your email whenever you like; until then it lives only in this browser, and the extension says so. For your key it stores only an encrypted record (Argon2id and AES-GCM), and each link you make is kept encrypted with a key derived from your account key.

WHAT IT DOES
- Make a payment. Enter an amount and, if you like, a claim password the recipient must also know. The amount goes into an escrow on the Stellar ledger, behind a fresh key made for that one payment. The secret that opens it lives only after the "#" in the URL, a part browsers do not send to servers. The link carries no amount (the claim page reads it from the ledger) and no name unless you type one in From. A name you type travels inside the link, after the "#", so anyone who can read the chat can read it.
- Follow each payment. Statuses: Waiting, Claimed, Reclaimable (unclaimed after 7 days, so you can take it back), Reclaimed, Closed (claimed or taken back, when we cannot tell which), Uncertain (sent but not confirmed yet; never sent again automatically) and Didn't go through (nothing moved).
- Copy the URL, open the transaction on stellar.expert, or take back an unclaimed payment once it is reclaimable.
- Right-click in a text box and choose "Paste a Lumenia link here". When the payment is ready, the finished link is inserted into that box, such as a chat box, an email draft or any ordinary text field. It only inserts text. It never sends a message and collects nothing from the page.
- Auto-lock. The unlocked key stays in memory and locks after 15 minutes of inactivity (you can choose 5, 15 or 60) and whenever the browser restarts.

PRACTICE MONEY FIRST
By default the extension uses practice money on the Stellar test network; the switch at the top changes it. Real money is only for wallets approved into the invite-only pilot, and it needs a password-locked account that is backed up. Before the first switch to real money the extension shows a one-time note: "Real money on Lumenia is an early pilot. It has not been reviewed by an outside security firm yet. You can lose money, so keep amounts small." Real money is capped at $5 a link and up to $25 a day from you ($50 a day across the whole pilot).

NOT HELD BY US
Non-custodial: the money sits in the escrow on the ledger, never with us. Our servers only relay transactions and pay fees.

WHAT LEAVES YOUR DEVICE
To restore or back up an account: your email address and the one-time code, to Lumenia's server; a backup is your key locked with your password, which we cannot open. To add practice dollars: your public key. To pay or take back: the transaction you signed. On real money only: your public key, to check whether the pilot approved it. For balances and status: reads from public Stellar servers. Also a few usage counts, such as "link created", with no URL, secret or page content. Servers see your IP address for rate limiting. No ads, no third-party analytics kit, nothing is sold. Details: https://getlumenia.com/privacy

"Forget this account" erases everything the extension holds on your device. If the account was never backed up, or a link you made is still open, it tells you first, because this browser holds the only copy and the only way to take it back.

version.approval_notes:
Lumenia makes a payment link from the user's own Lumenia account and shows whether it was claimed. The recipient opens the link on getlumenia.com and needs no extension.

HOW TO TEST (practice money, Stellar testnet, free, no account or email needed): 1) Open the add-on: "Get started", then "Agree and continue". 2) "No, I'm new here": a password of at least 10 characters, twice, then "Create my account"; practice dollars are added on their own. 3) "Make my first link": 0.10, "Make the link", "Copy link"; open the link in a private window and press "Take $0.10" (no wallet needed). In Links the row turns Claimed. 4) Right-click any text box, choose "Paste a Lumenia link here" and make a link: it is typed into that box; nothing is sent, the user presses Send. Optional: "Back it up" stores the encrypted backup with an email and a mailed code; "Yes, bring it here" restores it elsewhere.

BUILD: esbuild, not minified. The source zip rebuilds byte-identically: Node 24, pnpm 9.12.0 (corepack), pnpm install --frozen-lockfile at the root, then pnpm --filter @lumenia/extension build; output in apps/extension/dist/firefox. See apps/extension/README.md.

BASE64 IN THE BUNDLE: background.js holds (a) the WebAssembly of hash-wasm 4.12.0 (MIT, unmodified, as shipped on npm), used only for Argon2id, to derive the key that encrypts the account key from the password; 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is for this only; and (b) contract spec data (XDR) from @stellar/stellar-sdk 16.3.0. Neither is obfuscation; both match the npm tarballs.

NETWORK: only the six hosts in host_permissions (Lumenia's two sponsor servers, Stellar Horizon and RPC on testnet and mainnet), also enforced by connect-src. No remote code: the build fails on eval(, Function(, string timers, importScripts(, dynamic import( and HTML from strings. Real money (mainnet) is an invite-only pilot, refused unless Lumenia's server approved the account, capped at 5 dollars a link, 25 a day per sender and 50 a day across the whole pilot.

LINT: 0 errors, 1 warning (UNSAFE_VAR_ASSIGNMENT, innerHTML in popup.js) inside Preact 10.29.8's own dangerouslySetInnerHTML branch, which no source here uses (the build fails on that word under src/).

DEPENDENCY AUDIT: pnpm audit lists axios 1.18.0 and smol-toml 1.6.1 under @stellar/stellar-sdk; neither is in the package (the SDK's browser build uses feaxios, and the TOML parser is not reached).

DATA COLLECTION: required personallyIdentifyingInfo (the email for the one-time code), authenticationInfo (the code and the encrypted key record), financialAndPaymentInfo (the signed transfers); optional technicalAndInteraction gates the usage counters (an event name, two 8-byte SHA-256 hashes, the marker ext); withheld, no counter is sent.

PRIVACY: https://getlumenia.com/privacy#extension

release_notes.en-US: Links are private by default: a link no longer carries the amount (the claim page reads it from the ledger), and it carries a name only when you type one in From, after the #. From starts empty for every link. The one-time real-money note now says you can lose money, and the caps read $5 a link and up to $25 a day from you ($50 a day across the whole pilot). Real money needs an account made in the extension to be backed up first. A take-back the network has not confirmed yet stays open until the ledger shows it, and a paused service, a busy network and a spent daily fee budget each get their own message.
